Both disclosures present the table/details of In-Process Research and Development (IPR&D) assets from the VMware Merger, listing amounts released in specific fiscal years (2024, 2025) and expected release schedules (2025, 2026). The subject is the IPR&D release schedule from the VMware acquisition.

Both disclosures describe the 'VMware cloud foundation' product, defining it as a private cloud platform integrating compute, storage, networking, and management to enable infrastructure modernization and developer productivity. Although D080 also contains IPR&D table context, this specific product description matches D084 exactly.

peer_results.rationale: AMD's candidate disclosures either concern fiscal year structure (duration/dates) or general acquisition-related intangible amortization expense totals ($2.4B in 2024). AVGO's disclosure specifically details the release schedule and timing of IPR&D assets from the VMware merger. AMD does not provide a comparable year-by-year release schedule for specific IPR&D asset balances in the supplied text.

INTC's candidate disclosures concern fiscal year structure or licensed technology arrangement costs. Neither provides a comparable disclosure of future amortization or release schedules for IPR&D assets similar to AVGO's VMware-specific release schedule.

comparisons.peer_summary: Expected amortization expense for intangible assets is projected to be $67 million in 2025, $56 million in 2026, $52 million in 2027, $49 million in 2028, and $42 million in 2029.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose future amortization schedules for intangible assets, providing specific monetary amounts expected to be released or amortized in upcoming fiscal years. AVGO details IPR&D assets from the VMware merger, stating that $1,380 million of the $2,900 million balance is expected to be released in the second half of fiscal year 2025, with additional amounts expected in the first half of fiscal year 2026. Similarly, MU projects specific amortization expense amounts for its intangible assets, listing $67 million for 2025 and $56 million for 2026. While AVGO's disclosure is tied to specific released balances from a merger transaction, both companies use this section to outline the financial impact of intangible assets over the next two years.
